title: slot-starvation scratchpad: continuous-batcher throughput cliff
content:
Context:
- Personal troubleshooting notes. Intermittent throughput cliffs observed on continuous-batcher (CB) rollout on prod-like cluster. Suspect slot allocation / scheduling interaction with KV-prefetch and autoscaler burst settings.

Symptoms (what I saw):
- Total QPS for route /generate dropped from ~1.1k steady to ~360 during incidents while GPU pool utilization stayed ~60% (weird).
- p50 latency unchanged (~70ms), but p90/p99 jumped and tail tokens slowed.
- Logs show: "batcher_wait_time_ms increasing from 3 -> 120" and repeated `timeout waiting for batch` in runtime logs.
- Metric `active_slots` reported 28/32 but `slot_busy_time_ms` per slot ~0.
- KV-cache hit rate dipped from 85% -> 20% around the same time.
- Autoscaler did not spin up nodes; burst policy set to allowed but not used.

Initial quick hypothesis: slot-starvation (lots of slots reserved but not actually accepting work) due to continuous-batcher misconfiguration + KV-prefetch blocking threads while waiting for remote cache fetch, causing scheduler to think slots are free but they are blocked on IO.

Repro (toy) steps I used locally / what to try to reproduce under load:
1) Start local serving-runtime (image: canary/cb-test) with flags: --continuous-batching=true --batch-window-ms=8 --max-batch-size=16 --allow-burst=true --kv-prefetch=true --kv-prefetch-workers=4
2) Run loadgen: loadgen -q 400 -c 60 --seq-len-dist "short:0.8,long:0.2" --route /generate
3) Observe batcher metrics: prometheus query `sum(rate(batcher_wait_time_ms[1m]))` and `serving_slot_state{state="idle"}`
4) Toggle kv-prefetch to false and rerun; compare QPS and batcher wait times.

Commands I ran (snippets):
- kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runtime --since=15m | grep -E "batcher|slot|kv-prefetch|timeout" | tail -n 200
- curl -sS http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(batcher_wait_time_ms[5m]) | jq .
- gh pr checkout 3421 && make run-local RUNTIME_FLAGS="--continuous-batching --batch-window-ms=12 --kv-prefetch=true"
- python tools/loadgen.py --target-rps 1200 --concurrency 80 --route /generate --timeout 30

Representative error / log snippets (copied raw):
- [2026-02-21T14:12:33Z] runtime batcher: WARNING batcher_wait_time_ms=134.2 slots_available=28 reason="waiting for batch trigger"
- [2026-02-21T14:12:35Z] runtime slotmgr: DEBUG slot-alloc id=slot-22 state=reserved blocked=true blocking-on=kv-prefetch
- [2026-02-21T14:12:36Z] runtime kvclient: WARN prefetch miss for key=ctx-abc123 latency=98ms
- ERROR repeated: "timeout waiting for batch: 100ms threshold exceeded"

Telemetry snippets I pulled (promql outputs, abbreviated):
- sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (route): 360 (incident) vs 1100 (healthy)
- avg(batcher_wait_time_ms) 1m: incident=95, healthy=4
- kv_prefetch_worker_queue_length: spike to 240 at incident start
- slot_allocation_attempts_total: no corresponding rise -> indicates slots not being reallocated

Observations so far:
- When kv-prefetch is enabled with low worker count, prefetch queue piles up and prefetch workers block slots; the scheduler marks them as reserved but they are not eligible for new requests.
- Increasing `--kv-prefetch-workers` to 12 locally reduced the wait_time and improved observed QPS (simple smoke).
- But in prod, increasing prefetch workers might increase memory pressure per runtime pod, and interacting with autoscaler (pod CPU usage low) won't trigger more pods.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: KV-prefetch performing synchronous prefetch from remote store on initial token expand, blocking slot's IO path; batcher views slot as reserved and cannot use it -> effective concurrency is lower than reported.
2) Secondary: Continuous-batch wakeup threshold mis-set (batch-window-ms too low) causing the batcher to frequently spin and attempt to form batches but failing due to slot blocking.
3) Tertiary: Scheduler bug: slot state transitions (busy->idle) not being published correctly when prefetch is in-progress (race).
4) Less likely: Autoscaler config overlay prevents burst nodes from being provisioned because pod metrics used are CPU only; blocked slots are not CPU-heavy so no scale-up.

Quick experiments to run (ordered):
- A: Toggle kv-prefetch=false on a canary pool, run 30m smoke at 1k rps, collect batcher_wait_time_ms, QPS, slot_busy_time.
- B: Keep kv-prefetch=true but double kv-prefetch-workers; monitor memory/GC and QPS.
- C: Increase batch-window-ms from 8 -> 20ms to allow more accumulation and reduce wakeups.
- D: Add a synthetic metric for `slot_blocking_io` to get immediate signal.
- E: Change autoscaler to consider `requests_in_flight` metric (custom) instead of CPU.

Short config snippets I tried (k8s env):
- env: BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8
- env: CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=true
- env: KV_PREFETCH=true
- env: KV_PREFETCH_WORKERS=12

Notes / pitfalls while testing:
- Difference between `slots_available` and `slots_usable` is confusing in dashboards; add derived metric.
- When reproducing locally, ensure loadgen uses mix of short/long sequences; long sequences reveal slot holding behavior more.
- Watch for side-effect: raising prefetch workers increases memory; for small pods it caused OOM in one run (recorded).

Open questions / TODOs for next session:
- Confirm whether slot state is being flipped to `reserved` preemptively (race in scheduler). Add extra logging around state transitions for 10m window for canary pods.
- Validate autoscaler metric selection: open PR to add `requests_in_flight` as HPA metric for the cb-canary pool.
- Coordinate with infra to run an experiment where we disable kv-prefetch only on small subset of canary traffic; need feature-flag rollout change.

Quick timeline (as I saw it):
- 2026-02-21 14:10: incident start, batcher_wait rising;
- 14:12: prefetch queue spike, kv cache miss rate up;
- 14:18: manual toggle on test pod (kv-prefetch=false) -> partial recovery;
- 14:40: rolled back change to avoid memory regression;
- 15:05: incident resolved after autoscaler manual bump (but didn't fully explain cause).

Notes to self (short):
- Add `slot_blocking_io` metric ASAP before next incident.
- Keep downstream tests isolated: run cfg changes on pool with <=10% production traffic.
- Capture flame graphs for runtime during next run with prefetch enabled.

Sign-off: rough personal scratchpad. Will sync w/ Priya for coordinated canary tomorrow.
